newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: St Lukes faces higher funding costs.
newsitem.headline: St Lukes faces higher funding costs.

text.p: St Lukes Group Ltd chairman Bill Falconer said on Friday the shopping mall owner-operator faced significantly higher funding costs this year than at the time of its float in December, 1993.
"The funding costs of the company will rise significantly this year as NZ$40 million of debt turns over on Decmeber 13," Falconer told the annual meeting.
The favourable rates established at the time of the float (6.21 percent) had now been been rescheduled at new average rate of 8.9 percent, he said.
Elsewhere in his speech, Falconer said the company had an ongoing requirement for development capital.
The WestCity project was nearing completion and a decision on Glenfield was imminent. In the interim, the company was addressing upgrades of its Pakuranga and St Lukes centres.
The company's balance sheet remained in a strong position with a net debt level of 22 percent.
In the immediate future St Lukes expected to be able to meet its capital requirements from cash flow and available debt lines.

"Our intention is to maintain a conservative funding ratio, and should we decide to proceed with Glenfield it is most likely that we will need to approach the market for further capital during the course of next year," he said.
The dividend reinvestment plan had continued to be a useful source of capital, Falconer said.
Commercial Director John Syme said the outlook of 1996/7 remained positive.

"Although we expect to see a slowing down in retail sales for the remainder of this year, 1997 is expected to upturn with the build up of the July tax cuts and with tax cuts expected to be introduced in July next year," he said.
Syme said that the sale of the its Downtown Shopping Centre in central Auckland was expected to take place within six months.
